sentences.text: Tyrannosaurus possessed short but unusually powerful forelimbs with two clawed digits relative to its large hind limbs.
The Bucky specimen stood 10 feet tall and measured 35 feet long, while the Sue specimen ranged from 12.3 to 12.8 meters in length and 3.66 to 3.96 meters tall at the hips.
The largest known Tyrannosaurus skulls measure up to 1.52 meters in length.
The number of tail vertebrae in T. rex is unknown but likely numbered at least forty.
While the most complete specimen is 12.3 to 12.4 meters long, modern estimates suggest Tyrannosaurus could reach 13 meters in length, 3.7 to 4 meters in height, and 8.8 tons in mass.
Tyrannosaurus had the largest estimated bite force of any terrestrial animal.
Bucky is the first Tyrannosaurus specimen found to preserve a furcula, or wishbone.
A juvenile Tyrannosaurus specimen known as the Jordan theropod weighed approximately 30 kg, whereas the largest adult specimens likely weighed about 5,650 kg.
A 2017 study found that a Tyrannosaurus specimen nicknamed Wyrex preserves patches of mosaic scales on its tail, hip, and neck.
Soft tissue and proteins have been found in at least one T. rex specimen.
A tooth identified as Tyrannosaurus rex was found in July 1874 near Golden, Colorado, by Peter T. Dotson.
Barnum Brown discovered the first partial skeleton of Tyrannosaurus rex in eastern Wyoming in 1900.
The genus Tyrannosaurus was described by Osborn in 1905.
Starting in the 1960s, renewed interest led to the recovery of 42 Tyrannosaurus skeletons from western North America, ranging from 5% to 80% completeness by bone count.
In 2023, researchers supported the idea that theropods had lips based on facial and jaw foramina patterns similar to modern monitor lizards.
Modern representations show Tyrannosaurus with its body parallel to the ground and its tail extended to balance the head.
Top speeds exceeding 40 km/h are considered infeasible for Tyrannosaurus because they would require leg muscles comprising 40% to 86% of its total body mass.
Studies suggest Tyrannosaurus had rapid and coordinated eye and head movements similar to other coelurosaurs.
Tyrannosaurus was likely an apex predator that preyed on hadrosaurs, juvenile ceratopsians, ankylosaurs, and possibly sauropods.
Pathologies in T. rex specimens, such as a hole in the jugal of 'Wyrex' and tail trauma, are suggested as evidence of attacks by other T. rex.
Chemical analysis of tooth enamel suggests Tyrannosaurus may have occasionally scavenged marine reptiles and fish washed ashore from the Western Interior Seaway.
Histological analysis revealed that the juvenile Jordan theropod was only 2 years old when it died.
In 2022, Wiemann and colleagues used lipoxidation spectroscopy to show that Tyrannosaurus had an endothermic metabolism comparable to modern birds and higher than mammals.
Paleontologists Kenneth Carpenter and Matt Smith argued that Tyrannosaurus forelimbs were not useless and that the animal was not an obligate scavenger.
Analysis of very young Tyrannosaurus specimens suggests that if parental care occurred, it was likely limited in scope.
Tendon avulsion injuries were found only in Tyrannosaurus and Allosaurus among the theropods studied.
Tyrannosaurus rex is the type species of the genus Tyrannosaurus.
Daspletosaurus and Tarbosaurus are other members of the tyrannosaurine subfamily and have occasionally been synonymized with Tyrannosaurus.
Tyrannosaurus lived in western North America on the island continent of Laramidia during the Late Cretaceous.
Tyrannosaurs began as small theropods, with at least some becoming larger by the Early Cretaceous.
The juvenile skeleton 'Jane' was initially debated as either a pygmy tyrannosaurid or a juvenile T. rex, but is now re-described as the holotype of Nanotyrannus lethaeus.
Scientists have debated whether Tyrannosaurus was primarily an apex predator or a scavenger.
